Linker vs Loader

BASIS FOR COMPARISON LINKER LOADER
Basic It generates the executable module of a source program. It loads the executable module to the main memory.
Input It takes as input, the object code generated by an assembler. It takes executable module generated by a linker.
Function It combines all the object modules of a source code to generate an executable module. It allocates the addresses to an executable module in main memory for execution.
Type/Approach Linkage Editor, Dynamic linker. Absolute loading, Relocatable loading and Dynamic Run-time loading.

A linker is a system program that combines object modules produced by the assembler into a single executable program. A loader is a system program that places the executable program into main memory and prepares it for execution. Relocation is the process of modifying the addresses in a program so that it can run from a different memory location. Dynamic linking postpones the linking of some external routines until run time.

Disadvantages of Loader
• Complexity – implementation difficult due to memory management, relocation etc.
• Overhead – loading and relocation take extra time before the program can start.
• Memory usage – the loader itself occupies main memory.

Overlay is a technique that keeps only the instructions and data needed at a given time in memory. An absolute loader loads the object code at the address specified by the assembler. A relocating loader can load a program at any free location in main memory.

The effective address is computed as EA = base + displacement, where the base register holds the start address. Address binding maps logical address L to physical address P as P = R + L, where R is the relocation register.

Algorithm for pass 1 of a two-pass linker:
1. Read each object module and note its length.
2. Assign a starting address to each module.
3. Build the global symbol table with the address of every external symbol.
